newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Generale Bank sticks to independent stance.
newsitem.headline: Generale Bank sticks to independent stance.

text.p: Generale Bank, Belgium's biggest bank, reiterated it sees no need for a partner right now, despite recent calls for further consolidation in the Belgian banking sector.
"Our strategy is one of stand alone, but if there are opportunities we will study them of course," chief executive officer Ferdinand Chaffart said in reply to a question at a news conference.
His bank today announced that first-half 1996 group net profit rose 8.6 percent to 7.3 billion francs.

On Monday, Standard & Poor's said that the Belgian banking system remains ripe for consolidation, even though the sector has coped relatively well with the upheaval that has beset European banking systems in the past decade.
The Belgian banking sector got caught up in a wave of merger and takeover speculation at the start of this year, but no major operations have been seen so far.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
